verificationNote: GOLDEN FIXTURE — INDEPENDENTLY GENERATED. The `expected` numeric values below were produced by the CRA Payroll Deductions Online Calculator (PDOC), the Government of Canada's official reference calculator. The founder ran each of the four scenarios through PDOC on 2026-08-31 and manually transcribed the resulting `CPP`, `CPP2`, `EI`, `federal tax`, `Alberta tax`, `total deductions`, `net pay`, `CPP additional-contribution deduction`, and `taxable income for pay period` values from the CRA-produced result PDFs into this file. These values are NOT derived from Spectre code, are NOT derived from the future Spectre gross-to-net calculator, and MUST NOT be regenerated from Spectre output. The Spectre calculator is measured AGAINST these numbers — the fixture is the source of truth for correctness. Any future slice that adjusts these expected values must (a) re-run the scenario through PDOC, (b) attach the fresh PDOC PDF as evidence, and (c) update `sourceRetrievedAt` accordingly. The CRA PDFs contained BLANK Employee-name and Employer-name fields — no founder / employee / employer / account identifier is stored in this fixture.

howToVerify: 1. Open PDOC at the URL above.
3. Select the pay-period date from the case's `inputs.payDate`.
6. Enter TD1 federal claim from `inputs.tdCredits.federalClaim` and TD1AB from `inputs.tdCredits.provincialClaim`.
7. For scenario `pdoc-zero-claim-more-than-one-employer`, tick the 'This employee has more than one employer or payer at the same time' box which forces federal claim to $0 with no BPA credit.
8. For scenario `pdoc-additional-tax-alberta`, enter Additional Federal Tax = 50.00 and Additional Provincial Tax = 25.00.
9. Confirm PDOC's calculated CPP, CPP2, EI, federal tax, Alberta tax, total-deductions, net-pay, CPP additional-contribution deduction, and pay-period taxable income match the `expected` block below.

cases.description: Basic ordinary Alberta hourly Employee, biweekly, mid-year 2026 H1, no prior YTD, default TD1 (federal BPA + Alberta BPA only), no additional tax.
Alberta Employee with a NON-BPA-only TD1 claim (higher federal TCP + higher Alberta TCP), biweekly, 2026 H2 (post-July 1).

Alberta Employee with `additionalFederalTaxAmount = 50.00` and `additionalProvincialTaxAmount = 25.00`. Proves the additional-tax amounts are added AFTER `T4` / `T4Prov`, never modifying the formula base. Independent CRA result preserves the base federal + Alberta tax at 163.23 / 78.45 (identical to scenario 1) and separately reports the additional-tax total of 75.00.

expected.notes: Do NOT combine the additional 75.00 into the base federalTax / provincialTax fields. The independent CRA result preserves federalTax = 163.23 (identical to scenario 1), provincialTax = 78.45 (identical to scenario 1), and reports additionalTaxTotal = 75.00 separately. totalIncomeTaxDeductions = federalTax + provincialTax + additionalTaxTotal = 316.68.

cases.description: Alberta Employee with `claimZeroFederal = true` — the more-than-one-employer / payer TD1 checkbox that forces federal claim to $0 with no federal BPA credit. Alberta TD1 remains at BPA. This is NOT merely `federal TD1 = 0`: it is the semantic 'employee has claimed federal amounts elsewhere so this employer must not apply the BPA credit'.

expected.notes: Federal withholding is materially higher than scenario 1 (251.82 vs 163.23 — a +88.59 delta) because no federal BPA credit is applied. Alberta withholding is unchanged from scenario 1 because Alberta TD1 remains at BPA. The semantic fixture condition MUST be preserved: this represents the employee's more-than-one-employer/payer claim-zero election, not merely a numeric TD1 of zero.
